title: VOR Checks: 4-4-6-4, Every 30 Days

faa.title: VOR equipment check for IFR operations

hook: Your VOR hasn't been checked in 31 days. Guess what's illegal now.

scenes.narration: Preflight, I F R flight plan on file, and the avionics log says the last V O R check was... thirty-two days ago. The needle looks fine, kid. The reg disagrees.
Thirty-two days since the check. Can you fly this airplane I F R on the V O R today? Commit.
No — the check is good for thirty days. Why so often? Oscillators drift, and the error grows quietly. That needle is decoration until you re-check it.
The fix takes five minutes. Tolerances: V O T test signal, plus or minus four. Ground checkpoint, four. Airborne, six. Dual cross-check, four degrees between them. Four, four, six, four.

On a V O T, center the needle: three-sixty FROM or one-eighty TO — old-timer trick: Cessna one eighty-two, one-eighty TO. Then LOG it: date, place, error, signature. Not logged? Didn't happen — same rule as fish stories.
Eyes off the screen. The four tolerances, in order, and the four things you log. Go.
Thirty days. Four, four, six, four. Date, place, error, signature. The only free maintenance item on the airplane, kid.
From the V O R lesson — set the course backwards and the needle lies. What's that called?
Ninety-one one seventy-one. Short reg, long memory.

quiz.question: The VOR was last checked 32 days ago. To use it for IFR today you must:
choices: Perform and log a new VOR check first
Nothing — checks are good for 90 days
Have an avionics shop sign it off
Cross-check it against GPS in flight
quiz.explanation: 91.171 requires the VOR check within the preceding 30 days for IFR — and any pilot can do it and log it.

quiz.question: Maximum bearing error for an AIRBORNE VOR checkpoint:
quiz.explanation: Airborne checkpoints allow ±6°; VOT and ground checkpoints are ±4°. (91.171)

quiz.question: A valid VOR check log entry requires:
choices: Date, place, bearing error, and signature
quiz.explanation: 91.171(d): the person making the check logs date, place, bearing error, and signs it.
